original_test_intent: Verify that the same BMC supports the IPMI Get Self Test Results operation through both the host in-band interface and authenticated lanplus out-of-band interface, returning a correctly decoded healthy or explicitly diagnosed controller result without transport discrepancies.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify SUT/BMC firmware, GUID/device ID and ipmitool build; verify IB device/channel and OOB address both reach the same controller; collect baseline identity; execute `mc selftest` once through IB and once through OOB using secure transport; capture raw output, stderr, exit and timestamp; decode the self-test result and any device-corrupted/inaccessible code under the approved specification; compare controller identity and result across paths; close sessions without reset, log clear or write.
manual_activity: Engineering supplies accepted result codes and IB/OOB same-controller mapping; both read-only queries are otherwise fully automatable.
required_inputs: SUT/BMC firmware, device ID/GUID and expected same-controller mapping
Host IPMI device/interface/channel and OOB management address
ipmitool version and target-supported self-test result code/text decoder
Protected IB/OOB credentials, host key/TLS/network trust and allowed cipher policy
safety_requirements: Verify IB and OOB controller identities before comparing results
Use protected credentials and trusted host identity; do not expose passwords in commands/logs
Run only `mc selftest`; no raw write, reset, power, FRU, threshold or SEL clear
Preserve complete stdout/stderr/exit from both paths
Stop on wrong/different controller, transport/auth failure, unsupported/malformed result or decoder ambiguity; do not reset to force health
agent_execution_scope: Validate same-controller mapping, tool and result decoder
Run one read-only selftest on each interface and retain raw/decoded evidence
Report path/result discrepancy without applying recovery
Do not change controller state, expose secrets, bypass host identity, reset BMC, clear logs or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve self-test result-code semantics and same-controller identity rule
Review non-healthy or divergent results and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Both `mc selftest` operations match the source, but sshpass, disabled host-key validation and inline OOB password are unsafe; raw output also needs decoding and target correlation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run `ipmitool mc selftest` once through the verified host IB interface and once through protected lanplus OOB to the same BMC; capture and decode full results independently.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: IB and OOB selftest, Cipher Suite 17 source detail, result check and 5/5-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate both transports to one controller identity, decode each self-test result and compare raw result, completion and transport health without mutation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds controller identity, secure credentials, exit/completion capture, decoder and divergence handling.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Two successful shell exits can still reach different BMCs or return a non-healthy self-test code; raw per-path semantics are required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: IB access may be proxied or unavailable under some OS drivers, and textual ipmitool wording can vary by version while underlying result bytes remain equivalent.

project_override_considerations: If IB and OOB legitimately expose different logical MC instances, engineering must define the expected relationship instead of forcing equality. Any approved alternate cipher must be documented without weakening credential protection.

Complete secret-redacted IB and OOB stdout/stderr/exit/timestamps
Per-path decoded self-test result/code and equivalence comparison
No-write audit, discrepancy record and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The unique source consistently asks for the same read-only self-test through IB and OOB. Result semantics and identity correlation are supplyable prerequisites.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The commands and purpose are clear. Controller mapping and accepted result codes can be supplied, so both paths are fully automatable.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2228 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00011-V001: approve the SUT/BMC firmware and device ID/GUID mapping proving the host IB device and OOB address reach the intended same controller (or define the expected multi-MC relation), accepted `mc selftest` raw/text result and error-code decoder, ipmitool/driver/cipher requirements and secret-safe trusted transport.

review_improvement: Preserves safe dual-path automation while preventing wrong-controller comparison, credential exposure and false health from shell success without self-test decoding.
independent_technical_reasoning: The self-test operation is read-only, but its value lies in the controller-returned status rather than command exit alone. IB and OOB travel through different interfaces and can accidentally target different management controllers, so identity must be correlated before results are compared. A nonzero diagnostic code can be a valid protocol response but an unhealthy device result. These distinctions are fully machine-decodable and require no state change or user confirmation.
